paths.description: Homepage/overview and primary acquisition entry; tested visual hierarchy, consent, responsive preferences, performance, privacy, crawlability and memory.
Primary commercial listing and plan-selection journey; represents pricing, commitments and conversion controls.
Distinct dark visual campaign/AI product landing template.
Representative editorial/detail template used to inspect reading experience and structured/share metadata.

findings.summary: The overview remains light when the user requests a dark colour scheme.
findings.evidence: The prefers-color-scheme: dark screenshot is byte-for-byte visually equivalent to the default capture and still uses white/light surfaces; the CSS advertises a dark-related signal but does not retint this page.
findings.suggestedFix: Set color-scheme: light dark and define dark surface, text, border, image and browser-chrome tokens with prefers-color-scheme or light-dark().

findings.summary: The cookie notice obscures a large part of the primary content on every fresh load.
findings.evidence: Desktop captures show a fixed 765×166 region covering the hero; at 360×800 it occupies roughly the lower 280px and hides the primary CTA. The platform probe identifies the fixed full-width region.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a compact, non-blocking consent surface that preserves access to the core CTA, provides equal accept/reject choices, and can be dismissed without obscuring content.

findings.summary: Several CTA accessible names do not contain their visible labels.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse/axe label-content-name-mismatch lists six serious failures, including visible “Sign up now”, “Get Plus”, “Get Pro”, “Get Ultra”, “Get Basic” and “Get Standard” links whose aria-label text replaces rather than includes the visible label.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove redundant aria-label values or make each accessible name begin with and include the visible CTA text, adding context with visually hidden text if needed.

findings.summary: The plans and pricing template has no h1.
findings.evidence: The plans probe returned h1: [] and the heading list starts at H2, even though “Choose the Google One plan…” is the page’s visible primary heading.
findings.suggestedFix: Render the unique page heading as an h1 and keep subsequent plan/application sections in a logical h2/h3 hierarchy.

findings.summary: The overview fetches an excessive set of country flag assets and avoidable page weight.
findings.evidence: The HAR records 183 requests and 2.98 MB transferred; 146 image requests account for 2.39 MB. Individual below-fold country SVGs cost up to 278 KB, and the image probe reports 50 images without dimensions and 16 without responsive sources.
findings.suggestedFix: Do not preload every regional flag. Fetch/render flags only when the region picker opens, reduce/optimise SVGs, declare dimensions, and use responsive sources for raster content.

findings.summary: The page ships avoidable JavaScript on initial load.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimates 132 KiB of unused JavaScript; the HAR includes about 400 KB of script transfer, including two analytics/tag-manager bundles totalling about 316 KB.
findings.suggestedFix: Delay non-essential modules and analytics until consent/interaction, split route-specific code, and remove unused initial bundles.

findings.summary: Several browser-enforced defence headers are absent and the CSP permits unsafe evaluation.
findings.evidence: The headers primitive found no HSTS response header, no frame-ancestors/X-Frame-Options, no Referrer-Policy, and no Permissions-Policy. CSP uses a nonce and strict-dynamic but also permits unsafe-eval; Lighthouse reports a CSP inspector issue.
findings.suggestedFix: Add HSTS, frame-ancestors, a restrictive Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy; remove unsafe-eval after identifying dependent code. Verify whether HSTS preload is intentionally relied upon.

findings.summary: Tracking requests and heavy tag-manager code load before the visitor chooses a cookie preference.
findings.evidence: During the untouched initial load, the tracker primitive observed Google Tag Manager, Google Analytics and DoubleClick; the HAR shows 161 third-party requests and 2.90 MB third-party transfer while the consent notice is still visible.
findings.suggestedFix: Gate non-essential analytics/advertising requests behind consent, minimise vendors and events, and batch any consented analytics.

findings.summary: Several links use generic “Learn more” text.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse SEO identifies five links whose text is only “Learn more”, pointing to different cookie, AI, family and support destinations.
findings.suggestedFix: Use destination-specific visible link text, such as “Learn about Google One family sharing”, while keeping real href attributes.

findings.summary: The canonical URL conflicts with the selected locale/hreflang URL.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse fails the canonical audit because the rendered en-GB page canonical points to another hreflang location. The page probe reports canonical https://one.google.com/intl/en_uk/about/ while navigation resolves through https://one.google.com/about/.
findings.suggestedFix: Make each localized page self-canonical (or consistently canonicalise the redirect target) and ensure canonical, hreflang, sitemap and redirect URLs agree.

findings.summary: Below-fold regional decoration dominates transfer cost.
findings.evidence: The 146 image requests transfer 2.39 MB, dominated by country SVG flags that are not needed until the region selector is used; one 32px displayed flag has a 1200px natural width and the probe reports 16 images without responsive sources.
findings.suggestedFix: Lazy-create the region list and its flags on demand, optimise SVG paths, and serve assets at display-appropriate resolution.
